name: NorthWest Crossing
label: NorthWest Crossing
about_prose: NorthWest Crossing sits on Bend's west side, on 486 acres that Brooks Resources Corporation and the Tennant family began developing together in the late 1990s under a partnership called West Bend Property Company. The land had belonged to longtime owner Bill Miller. The first building lots went to buyers by public lottery in 2001, construction started in early 2002, and the neighborhood's residential build-out ran until 2018. Rather than sell large parcels to a handful of production builders, West Bend Property Company formed the NorthWest Crossing Builders' Guild and released individual lots to qualified local builders working under one shared set of design guidelines. That approach is why the streets carry a mix of Craftsman, Tudor Revival, Colonial, American Foursquare and Prairie-style homes, ranging from 600 to 3,400 square feet across cottages, duplexes, townhomes, second-story apartments and single-family houses, 1,335 residential units in all at buildout. The City of Bend wrote a mixed-use overlay zone specifically for the property, and every home is required to meet Earth Advantage and ENERGY STAR standards, with some homes reaching LEED certification or zero-net-energy status.

The plan follows new-urbanist principles. A grid of tree-lined streets, front porches, traffic circles, and a walkable center along NW Crossing Drive sit about five minutes by car from downtown Bend. The commercial corridor mixes restaurants, cafes and LEED-certified office buildings, anchored by The Grove, a 13,800-square-foot market hall that opened in May 2021 with nine food vendor spaces and the Waypoint bar. Compass Park, a five-acre circular park built in 2016 at the center of the plan, gets its name from its round shape, and it holds a playground, a picnic shelter that seats up to 100 people, and open lawn. It anchors the NorthWest Crossing Saturday Farmers Market, now in its 19th year and billed as Central Oregon's largest, running late May through late September with more than 150 vendors each Saturday from 10am to 2pm.

On the west edge of the neighborhood, Discovery Park adds 40 acres, including a 3-acre pond kept for irrigation rather than swimming or fishing, a fenced off-leash dog area, a community garden with 51 raised beds, and a natural play area. Its Outback Trail links to the wider network in Shevlin Park, 981 acres of old-growth ponderosa pine and high-desert canyon along Tumalo Creek that the park district has been assembling since 1977. High Lakes Elementary, Pacific Crest Middle School and Summit High School, all part of Bend-La Pine Schools, serve the neighborhood.

NorthWest Crossing is not governed by a conventional homeowners association. The neighborhood's own site puts it plainly, that it is not a homeowners' association. Section 7.2(d) of the Master Declaration, recorded with Deschutes County as document 2001-63854, bars the Architectural Review Committee and any successor non-profit from assessing owners or lots unless the declaration is amended first, and allows only a reasonable fee for performing a design review. The same section leaves room for a homeowners' association covering some of the lots to levy an assessment of its own, and Article 8 requires the developer to form an association for every planned development inside NorthWest Crossing, so a condominium or townhome pod here can still carry dues. What a buyer of a standard NorthWest Crossing lot does not inherit is a master assessment. Instead, an Architectural Review Committee, appointed by the original developers with input from Builders' Guild members and design professionals, holds authority over exterior changes. Under the neighborhood's CC&Rs and design guidelines, paint colors, landscaping, tree removal, additions and new construction all need sign-off before work can start. That review process is a large part of why the neighborhood still reads as one coherent plan more than two decades after the first lots sold. It also means a buyer moving in from a neighborhood without that kind of design review should expect less freedom to change a home's exterior without asking first.

The trade-off shows up most on Saturdays in season. Street parking around the market and the commercial center runs limited, and market guidance asks visitors to carpool, walk, bike or roll instead of driving, use the overflow lot at Summit High School, and lock bikes at the racks in Compass Park or near La Rosa rather than at neighborhood trees and sign posts. A neighborhood built around a walkable center trades some quiet for crowding right at its own front door for a few hours each week from late May through late September.

sources.publisher: Master Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for NorthWest Crossing, recorded in the Official Records of Deschutes County as document 2001-63854, hosted by NorthWest Crossing
sources.supports: The recorded declaration is a scan with no text layer, so the PDF was downloaded straight from the neighborhood's own site and its pages were rasterised and read directly, not summarised. Section 7.2(d), on document page 12, reads verbatim: "Neither the ARC nor a successor non-profit corporation shall have the right to assess Owners or Lots unless and until this Declaration is amended in accordance with Section 9.2 and applicable law. The foregoing shall not negate the right of the ARC or a successor non-profit corporation to charge a reasonable review fee for performing the review functions described in Section 4. In no event shall this Section 7.2(d) be construed so as to prevent the establishment of any homeowners' association(s) covering one or more of the Lots, which association has the right to levy assessments on member owners or lots, provided such association is established in accordance with applicable law." Article 8, on document page 13, reads verbatim: "Declarant shall, at the time of creating a Planned Development that is subject to these Declarations, form an Association with appropriate Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws for such Planned Development." Together these are why NorthWest Crossing carries no master assessment while an individual pod inside it still can.
